thread:
sanjay: Heads-up — after last night's release (merge CL 54321) we're seeing a ~35% drop in p50 throughput for mixed-precision models on small-sequence workloads (seq<=64). Repro in staging: batch_size 8 drops from 1200 toks/s -> 780 toks/s.

elaine: Oof. Is this the scheduler change that prefers fp8-int4 packing?

mike: I saw a slowdown too. Quick numbers from a local run:
```
make bench MODEL=redwood-mix-small PREC=fp8+int4 SEQ=64 BATCH=8
before: 1200 toks/s
after: 780 toks/s
profiler: hotpath spends extra 0.9ms in dequant path per token
```

ci-bot: CI perf-regression detected: improvement_threshold breached on perf-suite/mixed-precision/staging (regression +32% p50). Suspected merge: https://ci.internal/redwood/changes/54321

lee: Any bisect yet? Could be kernel-selector heuristics now preferring the 4-bit kernel for microbatches which has worse kernel-launch overhead + dequant overhead for short sequences.

mike: Did a narrow bisect: reverted CL 54288 (scheduler: prefer-mixedpacking) locally and numbers go back to baseline. So that CL looks suspect.

tara: We can't just revert without checking quality tests — that CL was enabling a quant profile that improved PMs for long seqs. Need a targeted rollback or a rollout constraint.

sanjay: Suggestions: 1) add a short-sequence guard to scheduler to prefer fp8-only kernels when seq<=128 and batch<16; 2) temporary canary hold for the CL while we iterate.

mike: Quick patch I tested: add heuristic weight = kernel_overhead / (seq * tokens_per_call) and prefer path with smaller weight. Patch reduced regression to <3%. Patch gist: https://gist.internal/redwood/short-seq-weight

ops-bot: Canary run started with scheduler-guard=true (10% of traffic). Initial telemetry: p50 back to 1180 toks/s on canary, non-canary still at 780.

elaine: Can we get a flamegraph? The profiler shows dequant work on the CPU thread taking extra cycles. Paste from pprof:
```
# pprof flamegraph snippet
0.9ms dequant_unpack
0.4ms kernel_launch
0.3ms kv_cache_lookup
```

mike: Looks like the mixed-packing path does an extra unpack step for int4->fp32 then re-quant for fp8 path, which kills short-seq perf. For long seq it's amortized and helps.

sanjay: Plan: (1) hold rollout of CL 54321 for now, (2) promote mike's short-seq guard to default, (3) add targeted e2e perf test for seq=[8,32,64] in CI to catch this. Can someone file the rollout hold ticket?

lee: Filed: RLH-321 (hold CL 54321). Added owners: @mike @tara.

tara: I'll own the perf tests and add a canary gating rule that checks both long and short seqs. Also will quantify quality delta for long sequences before any revert.

sanjay: Thanks. Follow-ups: mike will open a PR with the heuristic and unit tests; tara will extend CI perf-suite; ops will watch canary for 2 hours and report. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Canary summary after 2h: canary p50 1190 toks/s, baseline cluster p50 780 toks/s, error rates unchanged. No new alerts.

mike: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/changes/54567 — includes heuristic + tests + benchmark. Marking as WIP until QA verifies.

elaine: Great work. Once QA signs off we can re-evaluate rolling CL 54321 with the guard or try a smarter packing plan that avoids the dequant unpack on short sequences.

sanjay: Closing loop: this is a mixed-precision scheduling regression introduced by a packing preference change. Root cause: extra dequant/unpack overhead dominating for short sequences. Remediation path: short-seq guard + CI perf coverage.
